description: We’re building an interactive Mars survival map for NASA Space Apps 2026 to help astronauts explore safely and do meaningful science. We plan to combine real NASA terrain, imagery, weather, radiation, and hazard data into an easy to use map with routes, safety alerts, and a return to base feature. We’re looking for curious teammates skilled in coding, web maps, data analysis, Mars science, UI/UX design, or storytelling. Join us to make Mars exploration safer and smarter!
summary: On Mars, a radio message to Earth takes 3 to 22 minutes each way, so astronauts on a moonwalk-style EVA can't wait for Mission Control to tell them where to go or when to turn back. MarsCuff is a free web map of Jezero Crater, built from real NASA terrain and geology data, that plans a Marswalk for them. You place the habitat, add 2 to 5 science stations (or press Suggest to pick the best ones in reach), and MarsCuff walks the safest route around steep slopes, builds the timeline, and marks the Point of No Return: the last spot where the crew can still get home with a safety reserve. It then prints the plan as a wrist checklist, like the cuffs Apollo astronauts wore. A "science glow" shows where only a person can find answers: rock no rover has touched, ground too fine for orbit to see, and contacts that show which rock is older. Every number comes from a NASA dataset or a clearly labelled model.
details:
What it does: route planning across real Jezero terrain (slopes over the limit are blocked), an EVA timeline with a 20% safety reserve, a Point of No Return, science tasks at each station from the geologic map and Mars 2020 instrument methods, and a printable wrist cuff. A "Watch demo" button tells the whole story in about 30 seconds.

Benefits: mission planners can try a Marswalk in minutes; analog field teams on Earth can print a cuff, walk it, and check our walking model; classrooms get a free site with no login, to learn about Mars from real NASA data.

Tools: Python (rasterio, numpy) to process the data once; Leaflet in the browser.

Next: the same pipeline could run on NASA Moon Trek data to plan Artemis Moon walks.
